question.text: Ms. Priya Shah chairs the Investment Committee of Naman Capital (Cat II AIF) reviewing the Q3 FY25 NAV. Portfolio investee 'MedTech Labs' has been marked UP by 45% over Q2 based on a follow-on round at a higher price. From a valuation-governance standpoint, the IC should:

answer.text: Accept the mark-up automatically since a 'price of recent transaction' (IPEV method 1) is unimpeachable

Validate that the follow-on is an arm's-length round, confirm the IPEV method is appropriate, disclose the >20% quarter-on-quarter deviation to investors with reasons, and update PPM/methodology disclosures if applicable
Reject the mark-up because 45% in a single quarter is inherently suspect
Mark up only 20% to stay under the SEBI deviation threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: Price of a recent investment is a valid IPEV method, but its applicability must be tested — the round must reflect arm's-length fair value. The 45% quarter-on-quarter move exceeds the >20% deviation threshold and must be reported to investors with reasons (which can include changes in accounting practices, assumptions, projections, methodology, or approach). Methodology changes, if any, must also be appropriately disclosed. The Trap: Option A treats a recent round as unimpeachable evidence; the manager must still test whether it represents fair value. Option C blanket-rejects the mark-up without engaging with the method. Option D — capping the mark-up at 20% — is concealment, not disclosure. Note: The IC's role is governance over method selection and disclosure, not arithmetic suppression of NAV movement.
